environment.stream: B — explicit withdrawal lifecycle + Pepperstone/Dominion Markets/Vantage adapters

ci.lane: backend (manage.py test covers broker_intelligence + the ADR-governance test)

commands: Workflow stream-b-adversarial-review (12 lenses over the full diff, each finding adversarially verified)
expected_results: The Withdrawal projection carries EXPLICIT lifecycle states (CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, CONFIRMED, EXPIRED, FAILED) and stage timestamps; the FIRST email of a card confirmation-required withdrawal is CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, never COMPLETED; status is monotonic and never regresses; a rejected/cancelled/expired withdrawal has no completed_at and no positive duration.

A rail-less neutral (effective category UNKNOWN) non-completion lifecycle follow-up ADVANCES (never creates) the existing external withdrawal it references (pass 2b), restricted to UNKNOWN so an internal-transfer/deposit is never scanned; externality is asserted only by the opening event, so no advance can create or inflate a withdrawal.

Three deterministic adapters (Pepperstone, Dominion Markets, Vantage) authenticate the sender by exact registrable-domain match, classify the lifecycle from anchored phrases, never derive EXTERNAL from prose (line-anchored rail field only), never capture a URL/token or an external card PAN/bank number, and register only via the worker-only register_default_parsers; their broker-config rows are seeded DARK (is_active=False).

A PII-free synthetic Pepperstone GBP-15 card confirmation-required scenario runs end-to-end through the real parser and correlation engine: first email CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; idempotent confirmation/completion advance; out-of-order and duplicate deliveries produce no duplicate/inflated record; a missing confirmation never auto-completes (expires only on explicit evidence); an unrelated account can never attach.

Account/owner isolation holds (no cross-account attach); existing records, migrations and TradersWay/IS6 behaviour are preserved; migrations are additive and reversible; ADR-0079 is governance-unique; secret scan clean; no PII in the diff.
actual_results: broker_intelligence suite: Ran 816 tests OK (skipped 14) — 782 pre-existing + 34 new/updated (adapters, lifecycle, scenario, and the 8 review-regression tests). makemigrations --check: no changes detected in broker_intelligence.

ADR governance: core.tests_adr_governance 3 tests OK — ADR-0079 introduces no cross-directory duplicate. Secret scan: check_no_secrets — no findings. A PII self-scan of the new files found only the obviously-synthetic test account 70001234 (no real identifier; the Pepperstone scenario fixtures carry no account number at all).

Adversarial review (Workflow, 12 lenses, Ultracode): 6 unique findings, ALL CONFIRMED on verification; one earlier HIGH (is_active flip emitting an uncertified allowlist) was correctly REJECTED (the DARK is_active=False gate makes it inert). ALL 6 fixed and each pinned by a regression test: (HIGH) _TRANSFER_CLAUSE captured an external card PAN/bank number into the write-once destination_account -> restricted to internal-account-only, PAN-proof; (MEDIUM, LIVE regression) new CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED/CONFIRMED fell out of the metrics/withdrawal_speed pending bucket -> buckets widened + a status-coverage test; (MEDIUM) owner bridge in _find_by_reference could attach an account-resolved event to a DIFFERENT account's withdrawal of the same owner -> bridge account-scoped; (MEDIUM) the COMPLETED regex let a '#?\w{1,16}' token swallow 'to' and misclassify a confirmation as COMPLETED -> optional token tightened to '#?\d{1,16}'; (LOW) migration 0026 reverse bulk-deleted append-only audit rows -> reverse refuses to destroy activated/edited profiles.

Cross-app containment verified: the only non-broker_intelligence importers (trading/account_service.py, trading/account_removal.py) use broker_intelligence.services alias helpers, unrelated to the lifecycle/correlation; no other app consumes Withdrawal.Status or the correlation module.

Deviation (recorded in ADR-0079 + handoff): implementing the explicit states required a NEW advance-only correlation pass (2b); without it the new intermediate/terminal states are unreachable from realistic rail-less follow-up emails. Amber; preserves every safety invariant.
limitations: Repository-only / synthetic-only / DARK: no real withdrawal initiation/confirmation/modification, no Gmail/mailbox access, no broker portal/account access, no credentials/tokens/personal identifiers, no production or dev-DB mutation, no deployment/service restart, no public broker pages/publication, no Wayond/MT5/NAS/Tailscale change. PR auto-merge OFF; NOT merged without a separate Sponsor merge GO.

The three adapters are SYNTHETIC-calibrated (validated against committed synthetic fixtures, not a genuine broker sample) and their sender domains are the brokers' public brand domains, UNVERIFIED against real notification mail. Migration 0026 seeds them is_active=False so they never widen the live sender allowlist / authserv trust / catalogue reconciliation until an operator verifies the real domain + auth posture and activates them (provenance OPERATOR_VERIFIED) — a separate, host/Sponsor-gated step NOT in this packet.

External-rail withdrawals record NO destination account by design (an external card PAN/bank/wallet number is never captured — PII); only an internal trading-account number is extracted into source/destination_account.

Two EXISTING tests changed (called out): tests_correlation_lifecycle.py (the confirmation/confirmed mapping test rewritten for the explicit states) and tests_owner_attributed_withdrawal.py (three asserts updated from REQUESTED to CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED for the default confirmation-required event). No existing behaviour was weakened; the mapping is now explicit.

The dev DB was NOT migrated (no-DB-mutation hard stop); migrations 0025/0026 are proven against the migrated test DB by the unit tests. make check / make governance-check are run at finalize before the PR.
Streams C (public privacy pages) and D (MT5 telemetry + Wayond export) are separate PRs and are NOT begun.
